nodes.notes: Loop controller — releases 1 item(s) per pass. Output 2 (loop) processes the batch, output 1 (done) fires after the last batch. Watch out: Output 2 is the loop body, output 1 fires once after the last batch. Wiring these backwards is the classic mistake.

nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#content) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Space Out Posts
nodes.notes: Pauses 30 seconds — spacing calls to respect rate limits. Watch out: Long waits survive restarts, but the resume URL is single-use.

nodes.name: Mark Row Published
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Draft Tracker', matched on draftId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Count Published
nodes.notes: Collapses all items into a single summary item (for counts and run stats).

nodes.name: Cap Batch Volume
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 50 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Sort Drafts Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Tag Pipeline Metadata
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes pipeline, version. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Align Field Names

# Schedule the content calendar: Slack, batched

**Pattern:** Social Scheduler · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers captions work end to end across Slack and Google Sheets.

It moves through 16 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Read Content Calendar (Google Sheets)
3. Due for Publishing?
4. Post One at a Time
5. Publish to Slack
6. Space Out Posts
7. Mark Row Published
8. Count Published
9. Cap Batch Volume
10. Sort Drafts Newest First
11. Tag Pipeline Metadata
12. Align Field Names
13. Save Execution Metadata
14. Summarize Run Stats
15. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
16. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing captions work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Read Content Calendar (Google Sheets) → Due for Publishing? → Post One at a Time → Publish to Slack → Space Out Posts → Mark Row Published → Count Published → Cap Batch Volume → Sort Drafts Newest First → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Align Field Names → Save Execution Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Slack and Google Sheets aligned by hand for captions
- Captions sequences that run over days and must survive a restart before Slack
- A backlog too large to push into Slack in one pass, across 18 nodes
- Captions work where "Read Content Calendar (Google Sheets)" is still a manual step before Slack

## You get

- Keeps Slack and Google Sheets in step for captions, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Slack or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 18 nodes in this captions build
- The pause before Slack is durable — a captions run survives a restart
- Batches the work so Slack rate limits never break a captions run
- Every captions run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Slack

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Posts go out one at a time through a batch-of-1 loop with a Wait between each, not all at once — most social APIs rate-limit bursts, and spacing also just reads as more natural than five posts landing in the same second. A row is marked published only after the post succeeds, so a mid-run crash resumes cleanly instead of re-posting everything.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Change the spacing delay and see how total run time scales with calendar size.
2. Add a second platform and post to both for each due item.
3. Manually mark one row as already-published and confirm the filter skips it.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**The loop runs forever or exits immediately**
Cause: The loop output and the done output are wired the wrong way round.
Fix: Output 2 is the loop body; output 1 fires after the last batch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your captions process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole captions payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
